newsitem.title: USA: OMM, Marine Transport Lines agree to merge.
newsitem.headline: OMM, Marine Transport Lines agree to merge.

text.p: OMI Corp and Marine Transport Lines said Tuesday they have reached an agreement in principle to merge.

In a statement, the companies said OMI would acquire Marine Transport Lines, a privately owned company specializing in marine and transportation services, particularly in the energy and chemical industries.
Their boards have approved the merger in principle and the transaction is expected to be completed in January 1998, they said.
In connection with the acquisition, OMI plans to spin off as a tax free distribution to shareholders a subsidiary owning and operating its foreign assets.
The unit spun off will retain the OMI name and will be managed by OMI's current management. The merged OMI-MTL entity will use the MTL name and be run by MTL's current management.

In the merger, MTL shareholders will receive OMI shares in exchange for their stake in MTL. When the acquisition and spinoff are completed, OMI shareholders before the deals will own about two-thirds of the outstanding shares of the merged companies and all outstanding shares of the foreign company.
Former MTL shareholders will hold about one-third of the outstanding shares of the merged entity.
The transaction is subject to completion of a definitive purchase agreement, a favorable ruling from the Internal Revenue Service, and OMI shareholder approval.
The purchase agreement and filing for the IRS ruling are expected to be completed this month, and closing of the deal is expected in early 1998, assuming the ruling is received on time.

Craig Stevenson, chief executive officer of OMI, said the transaction will complete the reconfiguration of OMI into purely an international shipowner. Richard du Moulin, chairman and CEO of MTL said, the transaction will make MTL one of the largest ship management companies in the U.S. with projected revenues of over $100 million from ownership and operation of 36 vessels.
"We intend to launch a corporate development and acquisition program to become a prominent player in the global maritime industry," he said.
OMI, a major bulk shipping company, currently totals 33 vessels anad has on order order, four Suezmax crude carriers.
MTL, the oldest ocean shipping company in the U.S., owns and operates a diversified fleet of 22 ocean-going and coastwise vessels.
